ca_wall_street.blurb: Wall Street is a small Joshua Tree crag on the backside of Elephant Dome, found by walking around the right-hand side of the Red Burrito formation in the Roadside Rocks area beside Park Boulevard. It has eight routes: six trad lines and two top-rope climbs. Grades begin around 5.7 and 5.8, include three at 5.9, and reach the 5.10 range, so the wall suits climbers working through the moderate grades on granodiorite.

ca_west_point.blurb: West Point is a south-facing formation in the Lake Arrowhead Pinnacles of the San Bernardino Mountains, lying beyond the Main Meadow. It has eight routes, five trad and three sport. The grades start with a single 5.6, add three at 5.9, and finish with four in the 5.10 range, so most of the climbing sits in the middle of the scale. Because the rock faces south it takes plenty of sun. The walk to the base is rough and brushy.

ca_wheeler_gorge_east_gully_aka_cobble_c.blurb: The East Gully, nicknamed Cobble Choss, is a small sport crag in Wheeler Gorge along Highway 33 near Ojai, on the Central Coast. Its eight sport routes climb conglomerate, and the rock quality changes noticeably from one line to the next. Grades run from a single 5.6 through two 5.8s and two 5.9s to three routes in the 5.10 range. The gully is leafy and has a few views, with a trail up the hillside leading in from the creek bend.

ca_wonder_wall.blurb: Wonder Wall is a northwest-facing sport crag among the small outlying walls of Fairview Mountain, near Apple Valley in the High Desert. It has eight sport routes: one at 5.6, single climbs at 5.8 and 5.9, four in the 5.10 range and one 5.11, so the grades cluster around 5.10. The wall stays shaded from morning into the early afternoon, and the car is parked only about a minute's walk from the base.

ca_ponderosa_wall_black_tower.blurb: Ponderosa Wall and Black Tower make up one small crag in the Rattlesnake Canyon part of Indian Cove, Joshua Tree National Park. It has eight routes on monzogranite, mostly trad, plus one sport line and one top-rope climb. Grades run from 5.8 through two at 5.9, with five routes in the 5.10 range. The walk in passes Corral Wall, then cuts left through dense shrubs on small trails and boulder-hops up the canyon for roughly 400 yards.

ca_lower_muffins.blurb: Lower Muffins is a small cluster of three similar-sized sandstone rocks separated by chimneys, in the Falls Area of Castle Rock State Park in the South Bay region of the Bay Area. It has eight climbs: three sport routes, two top-rope climbs and three boulder problems. Roped grades run from the 5.7 range up to 5.11, while the boulder problems span V3 to V8. Most of the roped lines can be led or top-roped.

ca_slight_inducement_boulder.blurb: Slight Inducement Boulder is a single block in the Happy Boulders of the Volcanic Tablelands near Bishop, a short way up the canyon beyond the Serengeti area. It has eight problems from V0 to V3, mostly V0 and V1, in styles ranging from steep moves on big holds to vertical climbing on smaller ones. The easy problems are on its west-facing side, which makes the boulder a handy warm-up stop on rhyolite.

ca_west_side_2.blurb: This is one section of Fairview Dome, the granodiorite formation next to the canyon trail near Apple Valley in the High Desert. It has eight routes, seven sport and one trad, and nearly all are easy to moderate: one at 5.6, four at 5.7, two at 5.8 and a single 5.10. Broad stretches of low-angle rock characterize this part of the dome.
